newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus police block election chief from office.
newsitem.headline: Belarus police block election chief from office.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko sent police and OMON special troops into the electoral commission on Friday to prevent the top electoral official, who was sacked on Thursday, from entering.
Lukashenko fired election commission chief Viktor Gonchar after the two men clashed over the validity of a November 24 referendum in which the president wants to extend his powers.
Gonchar, accusing the president of breaking the law, had vowed not to leave his post. His secretary said by telephone that her boss was not being allowed into his office.
"He is standing in the corridor. There are lots and lots of OMON and police, I cannot say how many," she said.
Special OMON troops prevented anyone from entering the building where Gonchar's Central Commission on Elections and Referendums is situated in central Minsk.

Parliamentary deputy Sergei Kalyakin said earlier that police had thrown Gonchar and three parliamentary deputies out of the commission "by force". Witnesses said members of Lukashenko's security service had thrown him out.
An official from the national press centre, on the same floor as the electoral commission, said police had cordoned off the wing where the electoral commission is situated.
